description: Main Stage presentations at DEF CON 29, featuring groundbreaking research into Exchange ProxyLogon, HTTP/2 request smuggling, Apple AirTags, eBPF rootkits, mainframe container escapes, and agricultural cybersecurity.

talks.title: 2021 Our Journey Back to the Future of Windows Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: SafeBreach researchers analyze five years of Windows CVE patterns to predict recurring vulnerability classes and discover new zero-day local privilege escalations.
talks.summary:
Analyzing Half a Decade of Windows Vulnerability Data

To identify systemic weaknesses in modern Windows operating systems, SafeBreach researchers Tomer Bar and Eran Segal catalog and classify every reported Windows CVE from 2016 through 2021.

Discovering Recurrent Architectural Flaws

Statistical analysis reveals repeating vulnerability patterns across Windows kernel components, RPC services, and driver installation subsystems despite continuous vendor patching.

Weaponizing Patterns to Discover New Zero-Days

By systematically targeting recurrent flaw archetypes, the researchers uncover novel zero-day privilege escalation bugs in the Windows kernel and core background services.

Predictive Vulnerability Research Frameworks

The authors present predictive research methodologies and defensive validation tools to help enterprise defenders anticipate future vulnerability disclosures.

talks.title: The Agricultural Data Arms Race: Exploiting a Tractor Load of Vulns
talks.teaser: Sick Codes discloses critical vulnerabilities across the American agricultural supply chain, hacking smart tractors, farm telemetry APIs, and grain logistics systems.
talks.summary:
The Cyber Fragility of the American Food Supply Chain

Modern industrial agriculture relies heavily on precision telemetry, cloud-managed tractor fleets, and interconnected grain distribution systems vulnerable to cyber disruptions.

Auditing Smart Tractor Fleets and Telemetry Portals

Sick Codes leads an ad-hoc research group investigating smart tractor manufacturers, uncovering exposed administrative portals, hardcoded credentials, and insecure APIs.

Chaining Exploits from Soil Sensors to Supply Chain Logistics

Combining web vulnerabilities and embedded telematics exploits allowed the team to compromise farm management networks, manipulate agricultural telemetry, and control machinery remotely.

Coordinated Disclosure and Food Security Governance

The author reviews the high-stakes vulnerability disclosure process with agricultural equipment manufacturers, urging national security stakeholders to protect the food supply.

talks.title: New Class of DNS Vulns Affecting DNS-as-a-Service Platforms
talks.teaser: Wiz researchers disclose a novel architectural vulnerability in DNS-as-a-Service platforms like AWS Route 53, enabling cross-tenant dynamic DNS eavesdropping and data theft.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Shared Infrastructure of Cloud DNSaaS

Major cloud providers operate multi-tenant DNS-as-a-Service (DNSaaS) platforms, resolving billions of internal and external DNS queries across distinct customer environments.

Discovering Cross-Tenant Dynamic DNS Hijacking

Shir Tamari and Ami Luttwak demonstrate how an unprivileged cloud tenant can register arbitrary domain names within shared DNSaaS name servers.

Intercepting Internal Corporate Traffic at Scale

Exploiting name server collision allowed the researchers to hijack dynamic DNS updates, exfiltrating internal computer names, IP mappings, and Active Directory authentication tokens from Fortune 500 enterprises.

Cloud Provider Remediation and Resolver Isolation

The authors detail their coordinated disclosure across major cloud providers (including AWS Route 53) and present architectural mitigations to prevent multi-tenant DNS pollution.

talks.title: The Unbelievable Insecurity of the Big Data Stack
talks.teaser: Sheila A. Berta exposes critical security oversights across enterprise Big Data stacks (Hadoop, Spark, Flink), executing remote code execution on distributed analytics clusters.
talks.summary:
The Growing Attack Surface of Distributed Analytics

Enterprise Big Data stacks combine complex distributed components—including Hadoop, Apache Spark, Flink, and Kafka—to ingest and process massive telemetry streams.

Architectural Complexity and Default Insecurity

Sheila A. Berta demonstrates that speed-first architectures and loose default access controls leave internal RPC endpoints and worker daemons exposed without authentication.

Chaining Flaws to Achieve Distributed Cluster RCE

By exploiting deserialization flaws, unauthenticated job submission APIs, and command injection gadgets, an attacker can compromise cluster nodes and exfiltrate raw enterprise data lakes.

Hardening Big Data Pipelines

Berta provides comprehensive security baselines, network segmentation rules, and authentication enforcement guides to protect distributed analytics infrastructure.

talks.title: No Key, No PIN, No Combo, No Problem: Pwning ATMs for Fun and Profit
talks.teaser: Roy Davis evaluates modern retail ATM defenses, demonstrating physical bypasses, electronic lock manipulation, and safe compromise techniques that defeat recent security patches.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Commercial ATM Defenses

Since the pioneering jackpotting research of Barnaby Jack, ATM manufacturers have hardened network protocols, locked down USB ports, and upgraded safe electronic locks.

Auditing Modern Physical and Digital Lock Mechanisms

Roy Davis investigates the physical construction of retail ATMs, dissecting electronic dial locks, safe chassis tolerances, and interior cable routings.

Executing Physical Bypasses and Safe Manipulations

Davis demonstrates practical bypass techniques against supposedly hardened ATM safes, bypassing digital combination locks and accessing internal cash dispensing mechanisms without tools.

Actionable Countermeasures for Financial Institutions

The author provides retail ATM operators and financial institutions with physical hardening guidelines, intrusion sensor placements, and lock upgrade recommendations.

talks.title: Abusing SAST Tools: When Scanners Do More Than Just Scanning
talks.teaser: Rotem Bar turns static application security testing (SAST) tools and linters against developers, weaponizing malicious repositories to achieve RCE during source code scanning.
talks.summary:
The Implicit Trust in Static Code Analyzers

Developers and CI/CD pipelines regularly scan untrusted third-party code and open-source pull requests using linters, formatters, and static application security testing (SAST) tools.

Analyzing Unsafe Dynamic Execution in SAST Parsers

Rotem Bar audits popular SAST tools, discovering that many engines invoke underlying language interpreters, dynamic imports, or external binaries during AST generation.

Crafting Poisoned Repositories for Scanner RCE

By embedding malicious directives in configuration files, package manifests, or custom lint rules, an attacker achieves remote code execution upon the developer opening or scanning the repository.

Sandboxing Security Tools in the Development Lifecycle

Bar outlines essential containment strategies, including containerizing CI/CD linters and disabling arbitrary code evaluation during static analysis.

talks.title: UFOs: Misinformation, Disinformation, and the Basic Truth
talks.teaser: Richard Thieme delivers a historical inquiry into government secrecy, psychological operations, and disinformation surrounding unidentified aerial phenomena.
talks.summary:
Historical Inquiry into Government Secrecy

Following his acclaimed DEF CON 21 presentation, author Richard Thieme explores historical declassified documentation regarding unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP).

Information Warfare, Misinformation, and Covert Narratives

Thieme analyzes the intelligence community's use of strategic ambiguity, counterintelligence operations, and deliberate disinformation to obscure technical developments.

Epistemology and Societal Perception Management

The presentation examines how intelligence agencies shape public discourse, stigmatize investigative research, and manage narrative consensus across mainstream media.

Lessons for Hackers and Skeptics

Thieme urges researchers to maintain rigorous critical thinking, evaluate primary source documentation, and distinguish genuine technical anomalies from coordinated disinformation.

talks.title: Old MacDonald Had a Barcode, E-I-E-I-CAR
talks.teaser: Richard Henderson encodes the classic EICAR antivirus test string into QR codes and physical barcodes, triggering unexpected security alarms and system crashes across scanning hardware.
talks.summary:
The Universal Standard of the EICAR Test String

For decades, the standardized EICAR test string has allowed security engineers to safely validate antivirus detection engines without deploying harmful malware payloads.

Encoding Antivirus Signatures into Optical Formats

Richard Henderson encodes the EICAR string into physical barcodes, QR codes, and matrix tags, testing industrial handheld scanners, airport kiosks, and mobile inspection apps.

Triggering Antivirus Interception Across Embedded Devices

Scanning the encoded barcodes causes background endpoint agents to quarantine raw memory buffers, lock up point-of-sale terminals, and crash optical decoding hardware.

Input Validation and Endpoint Resiliency

Henderson highlights the critical need for robust input sanitization and graceful error handling when parsing optical telemetry across enterprise endpoints.

talks.title: SPARROW: A Novel Covert Communication Scheme
talks.teaser: Reza Soosahabi and Chuck McAuley introduce SPARROW, a long-range wireless covert communication channel operating over cellular LTE and 5G MAC layers.
talks.summary:
Limitations of Physical and Network Layer Covert Channels

Most wireless covert communication techniques focus on PHY-layer radio modulation or IP-layer encapsulation, both of which are easily detected by modern spectrum analyzers and firewalls.

Exploiting Cellular LTE and 5G MAC Layer Protocols

Reza Soosahabi and Chuck McAuley discover an operational sweet spot within cellular Medium Access Control (MAC) layer signaling and scheduling mechanisms.

Introducing the SPARROW Covert Protocol

SPARROW embeds stealthy data packets inside standard cellular control frames, enabling long-range, low-power data transmission between mobile endpoints without triggering carrier billing or intrusion alarms.

Detection Strategies for Mobile Network Operators

The authors outline behavioral anomaly detection metrics for cellular carriers to identify irregular MAC layer signaling patterns.

talks.title: Phantom Attack: Evading System Call Monitoring
talks.teaser: Rex Guo and Junyuan Zeng present the Phantom Attack, exploiting implementation flaws in Linux system call tracing frameworks to completely blind endpoint monitoring agents.
talks.summary:
System Call Monitoring in Modern Linux EDRs

Host-based security agents and EDR solutions on Linux monitor system calls (via `ptrace`, auditd, or eBPF) to detect unauthorized reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.

Discovering Inconsistencies in Kernel Tracing Subsystems

Rex Guo and Junyuan Zeng uncover architectural race conditions and state desynchronizations in how the Linux kernel handles traced system calls from unprivileged userland processes.

Executing the Phantom Attack to Blind Sensors

The Phantom Attack allows an attacker without root privileges to execute arbitrary system calls—such as file modification, socket creation, and process execution—while presenting completely benign telemetry to monitoring agents.

Hardening Linux Kernel Tracing Frameworks

The authors propose kernel-level synchronization patches and EDR detection enhancements to mitigate system call spoofing.

talks.title: TEMPEST Radio Station: Data Exfiltration via Electromagnetic Leakage
talks.teaser: Paz Hameiri turns computer display hardware into a software-controlled radio transmitter, exfiltrating data from air-gapped systems via unintended electromagnetic radiation.
talks.summary:
The Principles of TEMPEST and Electromagnetic Leakage

Electronic circuits unintentionally emit electromagnetic radiation during high-speed operations, creating side-channel leakage risks for highly secured and air-gapped environments.

Weaponizing Display Interfaces as Radio Emitters

Paz Hameiri develops dedicated malware that modulates screen pixel patterns and display cable signaling frequencies to generate controlled radio frequency (RF) emissions.

Receiving Air-Gapped Data with Commodity Radios

By tuning a nearby software-defined radio or handheld receiver to harmonic frequencies, an attacker intercepts and demodulates keystrokes, encryption keys, and sensitive documents transmitted over the air.

Defensive Shielding and Zone Interventions

Hameiri presents EM shielding standards, acoustic dampening, and software-level frequency dithering techniques to neutralize TEMPEST emissions.

talks.title: Bundles of Joy: Breaking macOS via Subverted Application Bundles
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle dissects CVE-2021-30657, a zero-click logic bug in macOS application bundles that completely bypassed Apple File Quarantine, Gatekeeper, and Notarization.
talks.summary:
Apple's Layered macOS Execution Protections

Modern macOS systems enforce strict security gates on downloaded software, combining File Quarantine attributes, Gatekeeper signature checks, and mandatory Cloud Notarization.

Dissecting CVE-2021-30657: The Shroot Zero-Day

Patrick Wardle investigates a critical logic flaw discovered in macOS Big Sur, where maliciously crafted application bundles lacking a standard `Info.plist` completely bypassed Gatekeeper.

In-the-Wild Malware Weaponization (Shlayer)

Adversary campaigns immediately weaponized this vulnerability, distributing unnotarized malware installers that executed instantly with a single double-click without triggering OS security prompts.

Defensive Lessons in OS Architecture and Logic Validation

Wardle examines Apple's subsequent kernel patches and shares behavioral heuristics for security analysts to detect anomalous bundle structures.

talks.title: Warping Reality: Creating and Countering Next-Gen Linux Rootkits
talks.teaser: PatH demonstrates utilizing extended Berkeley Packet Filters (eBPF) to create kernel rootkits without writing kernel modules, presenting defensive detection mechanisms.
talks.summary:
The Risks and Evolution of Kernel-Level Rootkits

Traditional Loadable Kernel Module (LKM) rootkits provide complete system control but risk crashing the operating system when kernel versions or memory offsets change.

Repurposing eBPF for Stealthy In-Kernel Persistence

PatH explores how extended Berkeley Packet Filters (eBPF)—designed for high-performance tracing and observability—can be subverted to manipulate kernel memory and hook system calls safely.

Manipulating Process State and Concealing Activity

Weaponized eBPF programs can dynamically alter file read operations, conceal processes from `ps` and `top`, and redirect network socket traffic without modifying kernel code sections.

Detecting and Countering Offensive eBPF Deployments

The author provides incident responders with auditing tools and kernel integrity verification frameworks to detect unauthorized eBPF program attachments.

talks.title: ProxyLogon Is Just the Tip of the Iceberg: New Attack Surface on Exchange
talks.teaser: Orange Tsai reveals a revolutionary attack surface on Microsoft Exchange Server, chaining pre-auth SSRF, authentication bypass, and post-auth RCE into ProxyLogon, ProxyOracle, and ProxyShell.
talks.summary:
Targeting Microsoft Exchange as the Enterprise Crown Jewels

Microsoft Exchange Server manages confidential email, calendar data, and directory trusts for global governments and enterprises, making it a premier nation-state target.

Discovering the Frontend Architecture Weakness

Orange Tsai analyzes the HTTP proxy architecture in Exchange (`HttpProxy`), discovering severe parsing inconsistencies between the frontend reverse proxy and backend PowerShell/EWS endpoints.

The Triple Exploitation Chain: ProxyLogon, ProxyOracle, ProxyShell

Tsai details his discovery of three complete exploitation architectures, demonstrating how pre-authentication SSRF and cookie manipulation yield SYSTEM-level remote code execution on fully patched servers.

Transforming Enterprise Email Security

The research prompted emergency out-of-band security advisories from Microsoft, CISA, and national cyber agencies worldwide.

talks.title: Hacking G Suite: The Power of Dark Apps Script Magic
talks.teaser: Matthew Bryant delves into Google Workspace exploitation, weaponizing Google Apps Script to bypass enterprise security perimeters and establish persistent cloud backdoors.
talks.summary:
Google Workspace as an Overlooked Attack Surface

While Google Cloud Platform (GCP) receives extensive security focus, Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) contains powerful, interconnected automation scripting capabilities.

Weaponizing Google Apps Script for Post-Exploitation

Matthew Bryant demonstrates how Apps Script can be weaponized to interact with Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, and Admin APIs on behalf of authenticated enterprise users.

Crafting Stealthy Cloud C2 and Data Exfiltration Channels

Using Apps Script triggers and web apps, an attacker establishes persistent, domain-fronted command and control channels running entirely within Google's cloud infrastructure.

Auditing and Securing Google Workspace Environments

Bryant provides security teams with automated auditing tools and OAuth token governance policies to detect malicious Apps Script projects.

talks.title: Taking Apart and Taking Over ICS & SCADA Ecosystems
talks.teaser: TXOne researchers audit the Mitsubishi Electric factory automation ecosystem, discovering critical vulnerabilities in engineering software, protocols, and PLCs.
talks.summary:
The Role of Mitsubishi Electric in Global Critical Infrastructure

Mitsubishi Electric Industrial Control Systems (ICS) power critical manufacturing, oil and gas, municipal water, and transportation networks across the globe.

Deconstructing Proprietary Factory Automation Protocols

Mars Cheng and Selmon Yang reverse engineer proprietary communication protocols and engineering software suites (MELSEC, GX Works) used to program programmable logic controllers (PLCs).

Discovering Critical Zero-Days Across the Ecosystem

The researchers reveal a chain of vulnerabilities—including unauthenticated PLC memory overwrites, protocol injection bugs, and engineering workstation DLL hijacks.

Mitigating Operational Technology Risks

The authors discuss coordinated disclosure with Mitsubishi and provide industrial defenders with network segmentation blueprints and OT intrusion signatures.

talks.title: Breaking TrustZone-M: Privilege Escalation on LPC55S69
talks.teaser: Laura Abbott and Rick Altherr break ARM TrustZone-M hardware isolation on the NXP LPC55S69 microcontroller, elevating privileges from Non-Secure to Secure world.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of ARMv8-M TrustZone-M

TrustZone-M introduces hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to low-power embedded microcontrollers, isolating sensitive cryptographic keys from general application firmware.

Auditing Secure-to-Non-Secure Transitions

Laura Abbott and Rick Altherr examine the hardware memory protection controller and Non-Secure Callable (NSC) function gateway implementations on the NXP LPC55S69.

Discovering Hardware Configuration and Firmware Flaws

By exploiting improper SAU/IDAU register configurations and memory aliasing bugs, the researchers bypass TrustZone isolation and execute arbitrary code in Secure world.

Secure System Design for Embedded Developers

The authors outline best practices for configuring ARMv8-M security attribution units and validating transition boundaries.

talks.title: Hi, I'm DOMAIN Steve, Please Let Me Access VLAN2
talks.teaser: Justin Perdok exploits User-ID mapping features in Palo Alto and SonicWall enterprise firewalls, spoofing domain identities to bypass network segmentation rules.
talks.summary:
User-Based Network Policy Enforcement in Next-Gen Firewalls

To simplify firewall rules, enterprise firewalls (such as Palo Alto Networks User-ID and SonicWall SSO) dynamically map IP addresses to Active Directory usernames.

Exploiting Probing and Authentication Interception Mechanisms

Justin Perdok investigates how firewalls actively probe endpoints via NetBIOS, WMI, or XML-RPC to determine the currently logged-on user.

Spoofing Domain User Identities to Escape Network Segments

By forging NetBIOS responses or manipulating authentication probes, an unprivileged user on an isolated VLAN can spoof high-privilege domain identities, prompting the firewall to open restricted routes.

Hardening Next-Gen Firewall Identity Mappings

Perdok outlines essential configuration guidelines, advising network architects to disable unauthenticated IP probing and enforce cryptographic endpoint verification.

talks.title: Phish in Modern Waters: Vulnerabilities in OAuth Device Code Flow
talks.teaser: Jenko Hwong demonstrates weaponizing OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant flows, creating phishing attacks that bypass MFA without fake login domains.
talks.summary:
The Convenience of OAuth 2.0 Device Code Flows

The OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant allows limited-input smart TVs and IoT devices to authenticate users via a short alphanumeric code entered on a browser.

Weaponizing Device Authentication for Phishing

Jenko Hwong illustrates how attackers initiate device login flows and trick target victims into entering the verification code on legitimate identity provider websites (such as Microsoft or Google).

Bypassing Multi-Factor Authentication and Conditional Access

Because the victim authenticates directly on the official provider portal, MFA challenges succeed normally, granting the attacker a persistent OAuth refresh token.

Hardening OAuth Device Flows and User Education

The author provides identity architects with policy recommendations, including restricting device flow authorizations and enforcing device context checks.

talks.title: Instrument and Find Out: Parasitic Tracers for High-Level Languages
talks.teaser: Jeff Dileo demonstrates developing parasitic runtime tracers for interpreted languages lacking native introspection, enabling low-overhead dynamic analysis and fuzzing.
talks.summary:
The Introspection Void in High-Level Programming Languages

While modern platforms like the JVM and V8 provide robust profiling and tracing hooks, many specialized or legacy interpreted runtimes lack dynamic introspection APIs.

Building Parasitic Dynamic Tracers

Jeff Dileo demonstrates injecting lightweight instrumentation logic directly into language runtime interpreters without recompiling target binaries or source code.

Extracting Execution Telemetry and Function Traces

Parasitic tracers hook internal bytecode dispatch loops, capturing function arguments, return values, and memory allocations in real time with minimal performance overhead.

Applications in Vulnerability Research and Fuzzing

Dileo illustrates how security researchers can use custom tracers to guide dynamic application fuzzing, discover hidden API routes, and analyze obfuscated scripts.

talks.title: HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse
talks.teaser: PortSwigger researcher James Kettle pioneers HTTP/2 request smuggling, uncovering critical implementation flaws when front-end reverse proxies downgrade to back-end HTTP/1.1.
talks.summary:
The False Assumption of HTTP/2 Transport Transparency

Web administrators widely treat HTTP/2 as a drop-in binary transport layer, assuming protocol translation to legacy HTTP/1.1 backend servers is security-neutral.

Uncovering HTTP/2 Request Splitting and Smuggling

James Kettle reveals that binary HTTP/2 framing allows embedding forbidden HTTP/1.1 newline characters, spaces, and duplicate headers inside pseudo-headers.

Exploiting Protocol Downgrade Mismatches (H2.CL / H2.TE)

When front-end reverse proxies downgrade malformed HTTP/2 frames into plaintext HTTP/1.1 streams, backend servers desynchronize, allowing attackers to poison caches, steal credentials, and hijack web sessions.

Hardening Web Infrastructure and Gateway Protocols

Kettle provides web architects with detection tooling, testing suites, and remediation guidelines to enforce strict RFC compliance across reverse proxies.

talks.title: Bring Your Own Print Driver Vulnerability
talks.teaser: Jacob Baines demonstrates how unprivileged Windows users can install vulnerable, signed third-party printer drivers (BYOVD) to escalate to SYSTEM on fully patched hosts.
talks.summary:
The Unprivileged Installation of Windows Printer Drivers

Point and Print features in Windows allow standard unprivileged domain users to install certified third-party printer drivers without administrative approval.

Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) for Spooler Exploitation

Jacob Baines demonstrates curating a repository of signed, historically vulnerable printer drivers distributed by major hardware manufacturers.

Escalating from Low-Privilege User to SYSTEM

Installing these vulnerable drivers onto a fully patched Windows target enables an attacker to exploit known driver vulnerabilities, gaining arbitrary code execution as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

Disabling Point and Print and Restricting Driver Installation

Baines outlines Group Policy configurations and registry mitigations to restrict printer driver installation strictly to administrators.

talks.title: Real-Life Story of the 1st Mainframe Container Breakout
talks.teaser: Ian Coldwater and Chad Rikansrud unite container and mainframe hacking to achieve the world's first container escape on an IBM LinuxONE mainframe.
talks.summary:
When Mainframe Architecture Meets Modern Containerization

IBM introduced containerized workloads (Docker/Kubernetes) to its enterprise s390x LinuxONE mainframe systems to modernize enterprise core banking applications.

Collaborative Exploitation Across Two Distinct Disciplines

Container security specialist Ian Coldwater and mainframe hacker Chad Rikansrud combine forces to audit container isolation on mainframe silicon.

Executing the First Mainframe Container Breakout

Exploiting Linux kernel capabilities, shared device nodes, and s390x hardware virtualization quirks, the team successfully escapes an unprivileged container, gaining root on the host mainframe.

Hardening Linux on z Systems

The authors present remediation steps for enterprise sysadmins running container workloads on IBM Z and LinuxONE architectures.

talks.title: PunkSPIDER and IOStation: Making a Mess
talks.teaser: Alejandro Caceres and Jason Hopper reboot PunkSPIDER, a massive global web vulnerability search engine scanning millions of websites for critical flaws.
talks.summary:
The History and Controversy of Mass Web Scanning

Originally funded by DARPA, PunkSPIDER operated as a public global vulnerability search engine before shutting down due to legal threats and terms-of-service disputes.

Rebuilding the Architecture: PunkSPIDER and IOStation

Alejandro Caceres and Jason Hopper present the next-generation distributed scanning infrastructure, capable of auditing tens of millions of web applications in real time.

Automating the Discovery of Critical Web Vulnerabilities

The scanner identifies pervasive SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and exposed backup files across municipal, educational, and commercial web applications.

Transparency, Policy, and Public Security Accountability

The authors debate the ethics of public vulnerability disclosure, urging the industry to embrace transparency to drive defensive remediation.

talks.title: How I Use a JSON 0-Day to Steal Your Money on the Blockchain
talks.teaser: Hao Xing and Zekai Wu disclose a universal zero-day deserialization bypass in Fastjson, exploiting Java web services to execute RCE and drain crypto nodes.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Fastjson in Enterprise and Blockchain Services

With over 23,000 GitHub stars, Fastjson is one of the most widely deployed open-source JSON parsers in Java web services and cryptocurrency exchange backends.

Bypassing Modern Fastjson SafeMode and Deserialization Blacklists

Hao Xing and Zekai Wu uncover novel class inheritance chains that completely circumvent Fastjson's security checks and AutoType restrictions.

Achieving Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution

Submitting crafted JSON payloads allows an attacker to instantiate dangerous Java gadget chains, achieving full remote code execution on target servers.

Targeting Blockchain Gateways and Remediation

The researchers demonstrate real-world attacks against cryptocurrency wallet services and coordinate upstream patches with the Alibaba Fastjson team.

talks.title: Worming Through IDEs
talks.teaser: David Dworken challenges the developer trust model by discovering critical vulnerabilities in modern IDEs (VS Code, IntelliJ) that execute code simply upon opening a repo.
talks.summary:
The Flawed Threat Model of Developer IDEs

Developers frequently clone untrusted open-source code under the assumption that merely opening and reviewing a repository in an IDE without clicking 'Run' is safe.

Auditing Extension Ecosystems and Workspace Trust

David Dworken evaluates popular IDEs (such as Visual Studio Code, IntelliJ IDEA, and Eclipse), analyzing automatic build triggers, language servers, and linter integrations.

Executing Arbitrary Code on Repository Checkout

By embedding malicious workspace configuration files and task definitions in a project, an attacker triggers silent remote code execution the moment the repository is loaded in the IDE.

Introducing Workspace Trust Boundaries

Dworken reviews industry responses—such as VS Code's Workspace Trust feature—and provides developers with guidelines for safely inspecting untrusted repositories.

talks.title: Privacy Without Monopoly
talks.teaser: Author and activist Cory Doctorow dissects Big Tech's false dichotomy between privacy and competition, presenting interoperability as essential for digital rights.
talks.summary:
The False Monopolistic Defense of Privacy

Dominant tech platforms argue that enforcing data interoperability and antitrust regulations would undermine user privacy, positioning their walled gardens as necessary security protections.

Deconstructing Walled Gardens and Platform Lock-In

Cory Doctorow argues that platform monopolies create systemic vulnerabilities, leaving billions of users captive to corporate policy shifts and mass data surveillance.

Interoperability as an Engine for Privacy and User Agency

Mandating adversarial and standardized interoperability empowers consumers to switch to privacy-focused alternative services without sacrificing their social graphs or data history.

A Policy Roadmap for Competitive Technology Ecosystems

Doctorow outlines legislative and technical proposals across the US and EU to foster open, decentralized, and competitive digital ecosystems.

talks.title: Breaking Secure Bootloaders
talks.teaser: Christopher Wade details actionable exploitation techniques to bypass signature verification in modern Android and embedded bootloaders, deploying unsigned firmware.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Secure Boot Verification

Secure boot chains rely on cryptographic signature verification inside primary bootloaders to ensure embedded hardware only executes authenticated operating system images.

Auditing Fastboot and OEM Bootloader Implementations

Christopher Wade investigates parsing routines, USB descriptor handlers, and memory layout constraints within commercial smartphone bootloaders.

Exploiting Parser Vulnerabilities to Deploy Unsigned Code

Wade reveals memory corruption and logic bugs that allow an attacker to bypass signature validation and flash custom, unsigned kernels onto locked devices.

Hardening Bootloader Verification Pipelines

The author outlines defensive firmware programming practices, hardware root of trust implementations, and bootloader fuzzing techniques.

talks.title: UPnProxyPot: Fake the Funk, Become a Blackhat Proxy, MITM Their TLS
talks.teaser: Akamai researcher Chad Seaman presents UPnProxyPot, a Golang honeypot that impersonates vulnerable UPnP routers to intercept and MITM blackhat proxy networks.
talks.summary:
The Exploitation of UPnP in Criminal Proxy Networks

Threat actors routinely scan the internet for routers with exposed UPnP services (UPnProxy), injecting port forwarding rules to transform consumer routers into anonymous proxy relays.

Building UPnProxyPot: The Golang UPnP Honeypot

Chad Seaman introduces UPnProxyPot, an open-source honeypot engineered to mimic vulnerable SSDP and UPnP daemon behaviors.

Intercepting and Decrypting Adversary Traffic

By posing as a functional proxy node in botnet networks, UPnProxyPot intercepts, logs, and MITMs encrypted TLS traffic routed through criminal proxy infrastructure.

Extracting Threat Intelligence on Active Cybercrime Campaigns

Seaman shares empirical data on cybercrime operations, credit card fraud rings, and credential stuffing attacks observed through the honeypot network.

talks.title: Sleight of ARM: Demystifying Intel Houdini
talks.teaser: Brian Hong reverse engineers Intel Houdini, the proprietary ARM-to-x86 binary translator for Android, auditing its translation engine and memory safety.
talks.summary:
The Role of Intel Houdini in Cross-Architecture Translation

To enable x86 Android tablets and emulators to run ARM-native mobile applications, Intel engineered Houdini, a proprietary dynamic binary translation engine.

Reverse Engineering the Houdini Translation Engine

Brian Hong conducts a comprehensive reverse engineering audit of Houdini’s internal just-in-time (JIT) compiler, instruction caches, and system call translation layers.

Discovering Vulnerabilities Across Instruction Set Boundaries

Hong investigates how Houdini maps memory permissions and translates ARM signal handlers, revealing subtle memory corruption bugs that break execution sandboxes.

Security Implications of Binary Translation Layers

The author evaluates the attack surface of cross-architecture emulators and translation runtimes in modern computing platforms.

talks.title: Defeating Physical Intrusion Detection Alarm Wires
talks.teaser: Bill Graydon demonstrates defeating supervised alarm wiring in physical intrusion detection systems, bypassing End-of-Line resistors and sensor loops.
talks.summary:
The Insecurity of Supervised Alarm Wiring

Commercial and residential intrusion detection systems rely on supervised electrical circuits to monitor physical door contacts, motion detectors, and vault sensors.

Understanding End-of-Line (EOL) Resistors and Supervision

Bill Graydon explains how alarm control panels measure circuit resistance and voltage drops to detect open circuits, short circuits, and tamper attempts.

Executing Non-Destructive Wire Bypasses

Using basic electrical tools and precision measurement equipment, Graydon illustrates how an intruder can measure loop resistance and splice parallel resistive bridges without tripping the alarm.

Modern Line Security Standards and Active Polling

The presentation outlines physical protection conduits, encrypted digital polling lines, and multi-sensor supervision to secure alarm communication lines.

talks.title: Offensive Golang Bonanza: Writing Golang Malware
talks.teaser: Ben Kurtz breaks down the mechanics of developing offensive Golang malware, demonstrating EDR evasion techniques, memory injection, and cross-platform compilation.
talks.summary:
The Rapid Rise of Golang in Offensive Operations

Golang has emerged as a preferred language for red teams and nation-state threat actors due to its static binary compilation, cross-platform support, and rich standard library.

Core Building Blocks of Golang Implants

Ben Kurtz walks through developing robust offensive Golang components, from in-memory PE execution to encrypted command-and-control (C2) communications.

Bypassing Modern EDR and Network Monitoring

Kurtz demonstrates techniques for bypassing endpoint detection, including dynamic API unhooking, direct system calls in Go, and obfuscating runtime symbol tables.

Defensive Engineering and Hunting Golang Implants

The author provides defensive analysts with Yara signatures and binary analysis guidelines to deobfuscate and reverse engineer Go binaries.

talks.title: Extension Land: Exploits and Rootkits in Your Browser Extensions
talks.teaser: Barak Sternberg exposes vulnerabilities in browser extensions, demonstrating how to weaponize privileged extension APIs into persistent browser rootkits.
talks.summary:
The Unchecked Power of Browser Extensions

Browser extensions enjoy sweeping permissions across visited web pages, cookies, and local storage, often operating outside standard web sandbox boundaries.

Auditing Extension IPC and Message Passing

Barak Sternberg analyzes inter-process communication (IPC) and `window.postMessage` handlers in popular extensions, uncovering severe input validation oversights.

Transforming Extensions into Browser Rootkits

By compromising an extension via malicious web pages, an attacker gains persistent access to browser storage, bypasses Content Security Policies (CSP), and intercepts plaintext keystrokes.

Hardening Extension Manifests and Defenses

Sternberg presents defensive development patterns and security auditing tools for developers to restrict extension API exposure and prevent cross-origin injection.

talks.title: The Mechanics of Compromising Low-Entropy RSA Keys
talks.teaser: Austin Allshouse explores mathematical factorization attacks against low-entropy and defective RSA keys in embedded firmware and IoT devices.
talks.summary:
The Fragility of Imperfect RSA Key Generation

While RSA encryption with sufficiently random primes is mathematically secure, flawed random number generators in embedded hardware yield low-entropy, factorable keys.

Mathematical Factorization Methodologies

Austin Allshouse reviews classical and modern cryptanalytic algorithms—including Pollard’s p-1, Fermat’s factorization, and the General Number Field Sieve (GNFS).

Scanning Global Internet Datasets for Weak Primes

By analyzing millions of public TLS certificates and SSH host keys, the author identifies thousands of shared factors and predictable prime distributions across live infrastructure.

Remediation and Secure Key Generation Practices

Allshouse provides guidelines for developers to audit hardware RNG sources and regenerate cryptographically sound RSA keypairs.

talks.title: Why Does My Security Camera Scream Like a Banshee?
talks.teaser: Rion Carter reverse engineers low-cost consumer security cameras, uncovering unauthenticated audio injection flaws and remote firmware takeover vectors.
talks.summary:
The Rapid Adoption of Smart Security Cameras

Connected consumer security cameras offer live streaming, two-way audio intercoms, and cloud storage, but frequently prioritize convenience over foundational security.

Hardware Teardown and Firmware Extraction

Rion Carter disassembles budget IP cameras, extracting SPI flash memory chips and dumping Linux root filesystems via UART serial consoles.

Discovering Unauthenticated Audio and Remote RCE Flaws

Auditing proprietary UDP audio daemons reveals missing authentication checks that allow attackers on the local network to blast arbitrary audio and execute root shellcode.

Securing IoT Connected Devices

The author provides device isolation guidelines for smart home users and recommendations for camera vendors to enforce encrypted audio channels.

talks.title: Rotten Code, Aging Standards, & Pwning IPv4 Parsing
talks.teaser: Kelly Kaoudis and Sick Codes disclose systemic IPv4 address parsing flaws across major programming languages (Python, Go, Rust), enabling SSRF and access bypasses.
talks.summary:
Decades of Inconsistent IPv4 Address Parsing Standards

Although IPv4 is the bedrock of internet communications, modern programming language libraries interpret non-standard IP formats (such as leading zeros and octal notation) inconsistently.

Discovering Discrepancies Across Language Runtimes

Kelly Kaoudis and Sick Codes uncover that Python's `ipaddress`, Go's `net`, and Rust parsers handle octal and hex notation differently from underlying operating system socket APIs.

Weaponizing Parsing Discrepancies for SSRF and ACL Bypasses

By supplying IP strings with leading zeros (e.g. `0127.0.0.1`), attackers bypass allowlists and firewall rules to target internal cloud metadata endpoints.

Coordinated Industry-Wide Upstream Patching

The authors detail the massive coordinated patch release across Python, Rust, Go, Node.js, and core operating system networking libraries.

talks.title: Reveal and Exploit IPC Logic Bugs in Apple Ecosystem
talks.teaser: Tencent Security researchers reveal novel IPC logic bugs in Apple's XPC messaging architecture, achieving privilege escalation and sandbox escape on macOS and iOS.
talks.summary:
Apple's Inter-Process Communication (XPC) Architecture

macOS and iOS rely heavily on XPC services for inter-process communication, using Mach messages to enforce sandboxing and privilege boundaries between user apps and system daemons.

Auditing XPC Message Deserialization and Verification

Zhipeng Huo, Yuebin Sun, and Chuanda Ding investigate how privileged daemons deserialize complex dictionary objects and validate client credentials.

Exploiting IPC Logic Flaws for Privilege Escalation

The researchers discover multiple logic vulnerabilities where privileged background daemons mishandle unverified client messages, enabling sandbox escapes and root elevation.

Defensive Architecture for Secure XPC Development

The authors provide Apple platform developers with secure coding standards for verifying audit tokens and validating XPC message structures safely.

talks.title: Timeless Timing Attacks: Exploiting Network Latency Without Measurement
talks.teaser: Tom Van Goethem and Mathy Vanhoef introduce timeless timing attacks, using HTTP/2 multiplexing to measure microsecond server execution differences over high-jitter networks.
talks.summary:
The Jitter Problem in Network Timing Attacks

Remote network timing attacks traditionally struggle over the Internet due to unpredictable network jitter and packet latency obscuring microsecond execution differences.

Introducing Timeless Timing Attacks

Tom Van Goethem and Mathy Vanhoef introduce a revolutionary paradigm: sending two concurrent requests inside a single HTTP/2 TCP packet to guarantee identical network transit times.

Measuring Execution Order on the Server

By observing which response the backend server returns first, an attacker determines which cryptographic or database query took longer, eliminating network jitter entirely.

Real-World Exploitation Across Web Applications

The authors demonstrate extracting cryptographic signatures, user existence oracles, and timing secrets across global Internet infrastructure without local network access.

talks.title: Vulnerability Exchange: One Domain Account for More Than Exchange Server
talks.teaser: Tianze Ding demonstrates chaining Microsoft Exchange vulnerabilities with Active Directory trusts, escalating a low-privilege domain user to full Domain Admin.
talks.summary:
Microsoft Exchange as a Pivot Point in Active Directory

Because Microsoft Exchange Server requires extensive Active Directory schema extensions and service accounts, compromising an Exchange server often provides pathways to full domain control.

Auditing Exchange Protocol Handlers and EWS Endpoints

Tianze Ding analyzes Exchange Web Services (EWS), RPC over HTTP, and Outlook Web App (OWA), discovering privilege delegation weaknesses in Kerberos authentication.

Chaining Flaws from Low-Privilege Domain User to Domain Admin

Using a single unprivileged domain credential, an attacker exploits Exchange impersonation rights and ACL misconfigurations to execute arbitrary commands as SYSTEM across domain controllers.

Hardening Active Directory and Exchange Deployments

Ding outlines detection strategies for anomalous EWS API calls and advises administrators on least-privilege delegation for Exchange service accounts.

talks.title: Hacking the Apple AirTags
talks.teaser: Thomas Roth (stacksmashing) glitches the Apple AirTag within days of release, dumping microcontroller firmware and re-flashing the device with custom Find My payloads.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Apple AirTags and the Find My Network

Apple AirTags integrate Ultra-Wideband (UWB) and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) microcontrollers to enable precision tracking through hundreds of millions of Apple devices.

Executing Power Fault Injection (Voltage Glitching)

Thomas Roth performs precision power glitching against the Nordic nRF52832 microcontroller during early boot, successfully bypassing Readback Protection (APPROTECT).

Dumping and Reverse Engineering AirTag Firmware

Dumping the internal flash memory allowed Roth to analyze Apple’s proprietary Find My protocol implementation and BLE advertisement beacon formats.

Flashing Custom Firmware onto AirTag Hardware

Roth demonstrates reprogramming the AirTag to modify broadcast beacon URLs, transforming the commercial tracker into a custom hardware beacon.

talks.title: Fuzzing Linux with Xen
talks.teaser: Tamas K. Lengyel leverages Xen hypervisor VM-forking and Intel Processor Trace to create an ultra-high-speed hypervisor-level kernel fuzzing framework.
talks.summary:
The Challenges of Operating System Kernel Fuzzing

Fuzzing complex OS kernels like Linux requires rapid state resets and accurate branch coverage collection without destabilizing the target system.

Leveraging Xen VM-Forking for Instant State Resets

Tamas K. Lengyel upstreamed VM-forking capabilities into the Xen hypervisor, enabling spinning up thousands of lightweight, copy-on-write virtual machine instances in sub-milliseconds.

Hardware-Assisted Coverage via Intel Processor Trace

Combining Virtual Machine Introspection (VMI) with Intel Processor Trace provides complete, non-intrusive instruction coverage telemetry without source code modification.

Discovering Zero-Days in Linux Kernel Subsystems

Lengyel demonstrates uncovering real-world memory corruption vulnerabilities in Linux filesystem drivers and system call handlers at tens of thousands of executions per second.

talks.title: I Know How to Take Over Your Kindle with an E-Book
talks.teaser: Check Point researcher Slava Makkaveev compromises Amazon Kindles by embedding malicious payloads inside e-book files, taking over devices upon opening the book.
talks.summary:
Amazon Kindles as an Overlooked Mobile Attack Surface

With tens of millions of Kindles deployed globally, e-readers contain Wi-Fi radios, internal storage, and linked Amazon billing accounts.

Auditing E-Book Parsing Engines and Formats

Slava Makkaveev investigates the proprietary Kindle document parser, auditing how the reader processes MOBI, EPUB, and Kindle Format 8 files.

Exploiting Memory Corruption in Book Rendering Libraries

Embedding a malicious font and script payload inside a standard e-book triggers a heap overflow during text rendering, executing arbitrary root code on the device.

Pivoting Across Local Networks and Account Takeover

The author demonstrates that simply delivering a malicious e-book to a user's Kindle allows attackers to steal account tokens and pivot across local home Wi-Fi networks.

talks.title: OTA Remote Code Execution on the DEF CON 27 Badge via NFMI
talks.teaser: Seth Kintigh reverse engineers the undocumented NFMI radio protocol on the DEF CON 27 electronic badge, achieving over-the-air remote code execution.
talks.summary:
The Mysterious Wireless Technology of the DC27 Badge

The DEF CON 27 electronic badge used Near Field Magnetic Inductance (NFMI) to communicate with nearby badges during the convention puzzle game.

Reverse Engineering an Undocumented Radio Chipset

With no public datasheet or protocol documentation available, Seth Kintigh reverse engineers the hardware registers, modulation schemes, and packet structures of the NFMI controller.

Discovering a Stack Buffer Overflow in Badge Firmware

Auditing the badge game firmware uncovered a classic stack buffer overflow vulnerability triggered upon parsing oversized wireless NFMI packets.

Executing Over-the-Air Shellcode

Kintigh demonstrates crafting a custom transmitter that broadcasts exploit packets, executing arbitrary code over the air on unpatched badges.

talks.title: PINATA: PIN Automatic Try Attack on EMV Smart Cards
talks.teaser: Salvador Mendoza introduces PINATA, a hardware attack tool executing extreme brute force attacks against flawed 4-digit PIN verification routines on EMV smart cards.
talks.summary:
EMV Smart Card Security and PIN Retry Counters

Standard EMV chip cards enforce strict PIN Try Counters (typically 3 attempts) before permanently locking the payment applet to prevent brute force discovery.

Identifying Flawed EMV Applet Implementations

Salvador Mendoza discovers defective smart card payment applets that fail to persist the retry counter properly across power reset cycles.

Building the PINATA Automated Brute-Force Rig

Mendoza constructs PINATA, an automated hardware rig that rapidly injects PIN combinations and resets smart card power lines within milliseconds.

Cracking 4-Digit PINs in Record Time

The author demonstrates exhausting the entire 10,000 PIN keyspace in under an hour, urging banking institutions to enforce strict non-volatile retry counter logging.

talks.title: High-Stakes Updates: BIOS RCE in Dell BiosConnect
talks.teaser: Eclypsium researchers disclose critical vulnerabilities in Dell BiosConnect, demonstrating TLS certificate verification bypasses to execute RCE during UEFI updates.
talks.summary:
Cloud-Connected UEFI Firmware Update Platforms

Modern enterprise PCs feature automated BIOS update mechanisms (such as Dell BiosConnect) that connect directly to vendor cloud servers over HTTPS to download firmware updates.

Discovering Flaws in UEFI TLS Stack Implementations

Mickey Shkatov and Jesse Michael audit the UEFI networking stack, discovering that BiosConnect accepts invalid and self-signed TLS certificates due to broken verification logic.

Executing Arbitrary Code Before OS Boot

By executing a machine-in-the-middle attack on the update traffic, an attacker injects malicious UEFI payloads that execute with Ring 0/SMM privileges, bypassing Secure Boot completely.

Coordinated Disclosure and Firmware Remediation

The researchers discuss coordinated fixes affecting 129 Dell models (over 30 million devices) and present firmware verification guidelines.

talks.title: Making the DEF CON 29 Badge
talks.teaser: Badge designers Michael and Katie Whiteley share the behind-the-scenes engineering of the DEF CON 29 badge, overcoming pandemic supply chain crises.
talks.summary:
Designing a Hardware Badge Amidst Global Semiconductor Shortages

Creating the official DEF CON 29 electronic badge required navigating severe worldwide chip shortages, delayed silicon shipments, and manufacturing hurdles during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Hardware Architecture and Artistic Concept

Michael and Katie Whiteley present the circuit design, power management constraints, and custom LED matrix hardware integrated into the badge.

Embedded Firmware and Interactive Puzzles

The creators detail the embedded microcontroller firmware, wireless communication features, and multi-stage cryptographic challenges hidden within the badge.

Lessons in Resilient Hardware Prototyping

The presentation offers valuable lessons for hardware hackers and makers on component substitutions, rapid prototyping, and embedded software testing.

talks.title: Response Smuggling: Pwning HTTP/1.1 Connections
talks.teaser: Martin Doyhenard introduces HTTP Response Smuggling, exploiting desynchronization in HTTP/1.1 response pipelines to poison caches and hijack user sessions.
talks.summary:
Expanding Beyond HTTP Request Smuggling

While HTTP request smuggling focuses on manipulating incoming requests between reverse proxies and backends, response handling pipelines represent an equally dangerous attack surface.

Introducing HTTP Response Smuggling

Martin Doyhenard analyzes how reverse proxies parse backend HTTP/1.1 response headers, uncovering discrepancies in `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` processing.

Poisoning Web Caches and Capturing Sensitive Responses

By smuggling premature HTTP responses into shared connection pools, an attacker pairs malicious responses with subsequent benign user requests, hijacking sessions and stealing credentials.

Defensive Architecture for HTTP Reverse Proxies

Doyhenard provides web application firewall (WAF) rule sets and connection isolation recommendations to eliminate response pipeline desynchronization.

talks.title: Wibbly Wobbly, Timey Wimey: What's Inside Apple's U1 Chip
talks.teaser: SEEMOO researchers reverse engineer Apple's proprietary U1 Ultra-Wideband (UWB) chip, analyzing its operating system, cryptographic ranging protocols, and security.
talks.summary:
The Introduction of Ultra-Wideband in Consumer Devices

Apple introduced the proprietary U1 Ultra-Wideband (UWB) coprocessor in the iPhone 11 and AirTags, enabling high-precision spatial distance measurement and direction finding.

Reverse Engineering the U1 Hardware and OS

Jiska Classen and Alexander Heinrich extract and reverse engineer the U1 real-time operating system (RTOS) firmware, mapping internal peripherals and memory layouts.

Auditing Cryptographic Distance Bounding Protocols

The researchers evaluate the security of the IEEE 802.15.4z secure ranging protocol, investigating potential relay attacks and time-of-flight manipulation.

Open-Source Tooling for UWB Security Research

The authors release open-source tools to interact with the iOS Nearby Interaction framework and analyze raw UWB packet telemetry.

talks.title: Hack the Hackers: Leaking Data Over SSL/TLS
talks.teaser: Ionut Cernica analyzes automated hacker tooling and exploit scripts, demonstrating how predictable exploit traffic leaks target data to network eavesdroppers over TLS.
talks.summary:
Predictable Behaviors in Automated Exploit Frameworks

Offensive security scanners and automated cybercrime exploit scripts frequently follow rigid, deterministic logic when executing payloads over encrypted networks.

Reconstructing Attack Logic from Encrypted TLS Metadata

Ionut Cernica investigates traffic patterns across popular exploit frameworks, analyzing packet sizes, TLS handshake parameters, and timing intervals.

Leaking Exfiltrated Data to Passive Network Observers

By reverse engineering the deterministic encryption padding and response handling of poorly coded attack tools, a third-party passive observer can reconstruct the stolen data.

Hardening Offensive Scripts and Threat Intelligence Applications

Cernica provides operational security guidelines for red teams and illustrates how defenders can apply traffic heuristics to detect automated attack tools.

talks.title: You're Doing IoT RNG Wrong
talks.teaser: Dan Petro evaluates hardware Random Number Generators (RNGs) across popular IoT microcontrollers, exposing broken entropy sources that compromise crypto keys.
talks.summary:
The Critical Dependence of Cryptography on Randomness

Cryptographic protocols—including AES key generation, RSA primes, and TLS nonces—rely entirely on unpredictable random number generators (RNGs) for security.

Auditing IoT Microcontroller Hardware RNGs

Dan Petro conducts rigorous statistical entropy tests across popular IoT silicon platforms (such as ESP32, STM32, and Nordic chips).

Discovering Zero-Entropy and Predictable Seeds

Petro reveals common software integration errors where developers read uninitialized RNG registers, resulting in fixed zero-value encryption keys and predictable nonce generation.

Best Practices for Embedded Cryptographic Randomness

The author provides developers with verified entropy harvesting routines, advising how to combine hardware noise with cryptographic PRNGs safely.

talks.title: A Look Inside Security at The New York Times
talks.teaser: The New York Times information security team shares the unique threat landscape facing investigative journalists, source protection, and operational security.
talks.summary:
The Unique Threat Landscape of Investigative Journalism

Major news organizations face constant, targeted threats from nation-state adversaries, surveillance actors, and cybercriminals seeking to unmask sources and intercept scoops.

Protecting Source Confidentiality and Digital OPSEC

Agent X discusses practical security protocols implemented in the field, from air-gapped workstations and burner phones to secure drop infrastructure (SecureDrop).

Technical Challenges in Modern Media Cyber Defense

The presentation examines defensive engineering challenges, including protecting mobile reporters traveling abroad, securing communication apps, and defending against targeted zero-days.

How the Hacker Community Can Support Free Press

The speaker invites collaboration with security researchers to improve open-source privacy tooling and defend press freedom worldwide.

talks.title: Glitching RISC-V Chips: MTVEC Corruption for Hardening ISA
talks.teaser: Hardware security experts execute electromagnetic and voltage fault injection on RISC-V silicon, corrupting trap vectors (MTVEC) to bypass Secure Boot.
talks.summary:
The Rising Adoption of Open-Source RISC-V Architecture

RISC-V is rapidly gaining traction across automotive, IoT, and high-performance computing, driving the need for hardware-level physical security validation.

Fault Injection and MTVEC Register Corruption

Damian Zabrocki and Alex Matrosov perform precision electromagnetic and voltage glitching against RISC-V microcontrollers during early boot execution.

Bypassing Secure Boot via Trap Vector Redirection

Corrupting the Machine Trap-Vector Base-Address (MTVEC) register redirects hardware exception handling to unprivileged code, defeating BootROM verification.

Architectural Hardening for Future RISC-V Silicon

The authors propose hardware-level glitch detection circuits, redundant execution registers, and verified BootROM architectures to secure RISC-V ISAs.

talks.title: Sneak into Buildings with KNXnet/IP
talks.teaser: Claire Vacherot demonstrates manipulating KNXnet/IP building automation protocols, unlocking commercial facility doors, lighting, and HVAC systems remotely.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of KNX in Building Management Systems

KNX and KNXnet/IP are standard automation protocols used worldwide to control lighting, motorized window shutters, access control, and HVAC across commercial real estate.

Reverse Engineering KNXnet/IP Communication Frames

Claire Vacherot analyzes unencrypted KNX frame structures, examining how building controllers discover and route telegrams over IP networks.

Executing Unauthorized Building Control Operations

By injecting crafted KNXnet/IP packets, an attacker on the local network or internet-exposed gateway can manipulate building environmental controls and open physical access doors.

Securing Building Management Infrastructure

Vacherot presents KNX Secure cryptographic extensions, network segmentation strategies, and monitoring tools to detect unauthorized building automation commands.

talks.title: Central Bank Digital Currency: Threats and Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: Ian Vitek audits Sweden's prototype retail Central Bank Digital Currency (e-krona), uncovering architectural vulnerabilities in Corda token implementations.
talks.summary:
The Global Transition to Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC)

Central banks worldwide are designing retail Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) to provide digital fiat currency with cryptographic security and offline resiliency.

Auditing the Swedish e-Krona Prototype

Ian Vitek investigates the architectural blueprint and Corda Token SDK implementation developed for Sweden's central bank (Sveriges Riksbank).

Discovering Flaws in Two-Tier CBDC Token Exchanges

Vitek reveals critical design weaknesses where malicious commercial banks or network intermediaries could manipulate offline transaction tokens and trigger double-spending.

Security and Privacy Governance for Digital Currencies

The author provides foundational architectural recommendations for central banks to ensure transaction finality, prevent systemic counterfeiting, and protect citizen financial privacy.

talks.title: The PACS Man Comes for Us All: Insecurity in Access Control
talks.teaser: Physical security experts expose critical vulnerabilities in modern Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), breaking OSDP readers and smart controllers.
talks.summary:
The False Promise of Modernized Physical Access Control

While facilities have begun replacing legacy unencrypted Wiegand badges with smart card Physical Access Control Systems (PACS), modern software-defined readers introduce new attack vectors.

Auditing the Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP)

Babak Javadi, Nick Draffen, Eric Bettse, and Anze Jensterle analyze the implementation of OSDP and Secure Channel encryption across major commercial access controllers.

Exploiting Installation Shortcuts and Firmware Flaws

The team demonstrates practical bypasses—from sniffing unencrypted master install keys over RS-485 to triggering relay drops via reader tampering.

Hardening Physical Access Control Networks

The speakers provide facilities managers with physical security checklists, including enabling end-to-end OSDP encryption and tamper-proofing controller enclosures.

talks.title: Robots with Lasers and Cameras: Liberating Your Vacuum
talks.teaser: Dennis Giese reverse engineers smart robot vacuums, hacking LiDAR, cameras, and firmware to liberate devices from proprietary cloud tracking via Valetudo.
talks.summary:
Smart Vacuums as Pervasive Indoor Surveillance Platforms

Modern robotic vacuums feature HD cameras, LiDAR spatial mapping, and Wi-Fi connectivity, continuously uploading domestic floorplans and video feeds to commercial cloud platforms.

Hardware Teardown and Rooting Techniques

Dennis Giese demonstrates hardware rooting methods—including UART probing, NAND glitching, and USB OTG firmware flashing—across leading robot vacuum brands.

Auditing In-Vehicle Telemetry and Camera Feeds

Extracting local firmware reveals unencrypted video storage and undocumented cloud telemetry beacons transmitting private household data.

Liberating Robots with Open-Source Firmware (Valetudo)

Giese presents Valetudo, an open-source cloud replacement that allows vacuum robots to operate fully locally on private home networks without external cloud dependencies.

talks.title: An Attack Surface Tour of SharePoint Server
talks.teaser: Star-V Lab researchers take a deep dive into Microsoft SharePoint Server, chaining multiple zero-day vulnerabilities to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.
talks.summary:
Microsoft SharePoint in Enterprise Collaboration

Microsoft SharePoint Server is a foundational intranet CMS and collaboration platform deeply integrated into Active Directory and enterprise data repositories.

Auditing SharePoint Architecture and Web Controls

Yuhao Weng, Steven Seeley, and Zhiniang Peng investigate internal SharePoint web controls, SOAP endpoints, and binary serialization formatters.

Chaining Authentication Bypasses and Deserialization Gadgets

The authors detail discovering multiple critical zero-days, illustrating how to bypass authentication filters and execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM via crafted serialization streams.

Hardening Enterprise SharePoint Environments

The presentation provides enterprise administrators with defensive auditing scripts and reviews Microsoft’s patch mitigations for SharePoint servers.

talks.title: eBPF, I Thought We Were Friends!
talks.teaser: Security researchers demonstrate offensive and defensive eBPF capabilities, manipulating kernel tracing data to conceal attacks and building resilient detectors.
talks.summary:
The Dual Nature of eBPF in Modern Linux

Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) has transformed Linux observability, monitoring, and security tooling by allowing sandboxed programs to run inside the kernel.

Manipulating Kernel Telemetry from Offensive eBPF

Guillaume Fournier, Sylvain Afchain, and Sylvain Baubeau illustrate how attackers can load malicious eBPF programs to overwrite function return values, manipulate socket buffers, and blind monitoring agents.

Building Resilient eBPF Security Monitors

To counter offensive abuse, the authors demonstrate designing tamper-resistant eBPF security frameworks that verify probe integrity and detect runtime code modifications.

Open-Source Detection Tooling Release

The authors release open-source eBPF monitoring tools to help incident responders detect unauthorized eBPF attachments in production Linux environments.

talks.title: Hacking Humans with AI-as-a-Service
talks.teaser: Singapore government researchers construct an automated spear-phishing pipeline powered by OpenAI's GPT-3 API, comparing AI-generated phishing to human campaigns.
talks.summary:
The Weaponization of Large Language Models

The emergence of AI-as-a-Service (AIaaS) APIs—such as OpenAI's GPT-3—enables generating convincing, context-aware synthetic text at massive scale and minimal cost.

Constructing an Automated AI Spear-Phishing Pipeline

Eugene Lim, Glenice Tan, and Tan Kee Hock build an end-to-end automated phishing pipeline that scrapes target OSINT data and generates hyper-personalized phishing emails.

Empirical Comparative Testing Against Human Phishers

In controlled authorized testing across hundreds of subjects, the AI-generated phishing emails achieved click-through rates rivaling and occasionally exceeding expert human social engineers.

Defensive Verification in the Age of Synthetic Content

The authors discuss defensive countermeasures, automated linguistic anomaly detection, and training programs to prepare organizations for AI-driven deception.

talks.title: Use of Offensive Enclaves in Adversarial Operations
talks.teaser: Dimitry Snezhkov explores executing offensive tradecraft inside Intel SGX secure enclaves, hiding malware payloads and decryption keys from host EDR sensors.
talks.summary:
Hardware-Enforced Memory Encryption in Modern CPUs

Hardware secure enclaves (such as Intel SGX) provide encrypted memory regions (Enclave Page Cache) designed to protect confidential application data from untrusted host operating systems.

Repurposing Secure Enclaves for Offensive Persistence

Dimitry Snezhkov investigates running offensive tooling inside SGX enclaves, shielding malicious code and C2 communications from host hypervisors and EDR memory scanners.

Executing Covert In-Enclave Cryptographic Payloads

Because host monitoring tools cannot inspect encrypted enclave memory, ransomware and implant modules execute stealthily with zero host telemetry leakage.

Defending Host Platforms Against Rogue Enclaves

The author outlines hardware attestation requirements, kernel driver restrictions, and host auditing policies to prevent unverified enclave execution.

talks.title: Racketeer Toolkit: Prototyping Controlled Ransomware Ops
talks.teaser: Dimitry Snezhkov introduces Racketeer, a modular adversary emulation framework designed to safely simulate end-to-end ransomware operations and test SOC response.
talks.summary:
The Need for Controlled Ransomware Simulation

While ransomware remains one of the highest-impact cyber threats facing enterprises, organizations lack safe, realistic tools to test detection pipelines and incident response playbooks.

Architecture of the Racketeer Toolkit

Dimitry Snezhkov introduces Racketeer, an open-source offensive agent and C2 framework engineered specifically for controlled extortion and encryption simulations.

Simulating Multi-Stage Extortion Campaigns Safely

Racketeer demonstrates realistic discovery, shadow copy deletion, network share discovery, and reversible cryptographic file locking with fail-safe key escrow.

Measuring SOC Detection Capabilities and IR Readiness

The author shows how red and blue teams can use Racketeer to validate EDR behavior rules, quantify MTTD/MTTR metrics, and train security operation centers.

talks.title: Time Turner: Hacking RF Attendance Systems to Be in Two Places at Once
talks.teaser: Vivek Nair reverse engineers university RF wireless classroom attendance trackers, building an Arduino spoofing device to simulate physical presence in two lectures simultaneously.
talks.summary:
Automated RF Attendance Tracking Systems

Universities and corporate facilities increasingly deploy proprietary wireless attendance tracking beacons to monitor physical presence in lecture halls.

Reverse Engineering Proprietary RF Beacons

Vivek Nair analyzes the RF physical layer and packet transmission protocols used by commercial classroom attendance devices using a software-defined radio.

Building the Time Turner Hardware Spoofing Device

By capturing challenge-response packets and identifying lack of timestamp validation, Nair programs an inconspicuous battery-powered Arduino device to emulate student badges.

Demonstrating Simultaneous Multi-Class Attendance

The project demonstrates successfully registering attendance across multiple simultaneous lectures, highlighting protocol flaws in contactless physical presence systems.

talks.title: Do No Harm: Healthcare Cybersecurity in Crisis (Panel)
talks.teaser: Clinical cyber experts debate the escalating impact of ransomware attacks on hospital clinical care, ICU mortality rates, and national healthcare resiliency.
talks.summary:
The Escalating Crisis of Healthcare Cyber Attacks

During a global pandemic, ransomware gangs relentlessly targeted clinical health systems, causing emergency room diversions and catastrophic outages in critical medical devices.

The Direct Link Between Cyber Attacks and Clinical Outcomes

Physicians Christian Dameff and Jeff Tully present empirical research demonstrating measurable increases in patient mortality during hospital cyber disruptions.

Federal Policy Interventions and National Healthcare Defense

Policy leaders Jessica Wilkerson and Josh Corman discuss federal initiatives (CISA, FDA) to mandate minimum cyber standards across medical device manufacturers and hospital networks.

Building Resilient Clinical Cyber Defense Coalitions

The panel calls for unified action across cybersecurity researchers, government agencies, and clinical staff to safeguard healthcare infrastructure.

talks.title: Do No Harm: Healthcare Cybersecurity in Crisis (Live Q&A)
talks.teaser: Dr. Christian Dameff, Dr. Jeff Tully, Jessica Wilkerson, and Josh Corman answer live community questions on protecting hospitals from cyber extortion.
talks.summary:
Live Community Q&A on Healthcare Cybersecurity

Following the panel presentation, the authors engage with the DEF CON community in a live session on protecting healthcare facilities from cyber threats.

Addressing Practical Clinical Security Challenges

The speakers answer questions regarding medical device patch management, clinical workflow continuity during network outages, and open-source medical security research.

Opportunities for Security Researcher Engagement

The panel provides concrete guidance for security professionals to volunteer with local healthcare providers and participate in medical device coordinated disclosure programs.

talks.title: Gone Apple Pickin': Red Teaming macOS Environments in 2021
talks.teaser: Cedric Owens details modern attack paths in non-Active Directory macOS environments, including Gatekeeper bypasses, cloud IdaaS targeting, and post-exploitation tradecraft.
talks.summary:
Attacking macOS Enterprise Environments

While most enterprise environments traditionally rely on Active Directory and Windows, many modern technology companies operate predominantly on macOS managed via cloud and identity-as-a-service (IdaaS) platforms.

Initial Access and Gatekeeper Bypasses

Cedric Owens explores common attack surfaces in macOS deployments, detailing weaponization techniques and a novel Gatekeeper bypass vulnerability used to execute untrusted payloads without user warnings.

Post-Exploitation and Lateral Movement

The presentation covers post-exploitation methodology tailored for macOS endpoints, including credential access, bypassing Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC), and pivoting through CI/CD pipelines.

Detection Opportunities and Defensive Hardening

Owens highlights high-signal telemetry sources for defenders, providing actionable detection strategies and behavioral analytics to catch macOS offensive operations.

talks.title: Using M(achine)ITM to Attack Active Directory
talks.teaser: Researchers reveal machine-in-the-middle attacks targeting Active Directory authentication protocols, extending relay attacks beyond NTLM to Kerberos and hybrid environments.
talks.summary:
Machine-in-the-Middle on Active Directory Protocols

Adversaries have long leveraged Machine-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks against Windows authentication, exploiting the lack of mutual authentication and cryptographic signing across legacy network protocols.

Relay Attacks Beyond NTLM

Sagi Sheinfeld, Eyal Karni, and Yaron Zinar demonstrate that credential relay attacks are not restricted to NTLM, revealing novel injection techniques targeting Kerberos authentication workflows.

Compromising Critical and Hybrid Infrastructure

The speakers detail attack vectors that compromise client systems, domain-joined Unix machines, virtualization clusters, and hybrid cloud Active Directory deployments to achieve remote code execution.

Mitigation and Defensive Guidance

The authors present defensive recommendations, auditing procedures, and protocol hardening configurations to neutralize machine-in-the-middle relay threats across enterprise networks.

talks.title: DoS  Denial of Shopping: Analyzing and Exploiting  Shopping Cart Systems
talks.teaser: How supermarket cart locks can be analyzed and abused as a shopping-system denial path.
talks.summary:
In this talk on the DEF CON 29 Main Stage, Joseph Gabay delivers "DoS Denial of Shopping: Analyzing and Exploiting Physical Shopping Cart Immobilization Systems," exploring the reverse engineering and radio exploitation of supermarket cart theft-prevention mechanisms. He opens at 03:00 by explaining the electromagnetic architecture of perimeter boundary wire loops buried beneath parking lot asphalt, which broadcast continuous low-frequency magnetic signals.

Joseph details the mechanical and electrical teardown of a cart caster wheel assembly at 06:00, exposing the internal inductive sensing coil, microcode controller, and spring-loaded locking solenoid. At 09:00, he describes the challenge of capturing very-low-frequency (VLF) 8 kHz signals with conventional Software-Defined Radios (SDR), illustrating how impedance mismatches and antenna dimensions complicate monitoring.

At 12:00, Joseph analyzes demodulated command waveforms, revealing how specific pulse durations trigger wheel locking. He demonstrates a novel attack vector at 15:00, utilizing an ordinary smartphone audio jack and speaker coil as a low-frequency inductive antenna to broadcast crafted signals. After decoding the three-pulse frequency-shift keying (FSK) command structure at 18:00, he concludes at 21:00 by addressing ethical implications and responsible disclosure to retail security vendors. talks.title: Bring Your Own Print Driver Vulnerability
talks.teaser: Abusing Windows print driver installation as a path from low privilege toward SYSTEM.
talks.summary:
Security researcher Jake from SafeBreach presents "Bring Your Own Print Driver Vulnerability" on the DEF CON 29 Main Stage, introducing a novel local privilege escalation (LPE) technique that weaponizes legitimately signed, third-party printer drivers to elevate privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on modern Windows installations.

[09:59] Jake explores the security model of the Windows Print Spooler service (spoolsv.exe), which operates under the high-privilege SYSTEM context. He explains that while recent zero-days like PrintNightmare highlighted native spooler vulnerabilities, administrative policies and Microsoft patches often restrict remote point-and-print features. However, low-privileged local users frequently retain the right to add printers and load driver packages.

[21:07] The presentation details the "Bring Your Own Driver" attack concept. Rather than attacking the Windows OS itself, an attacker supplies an older, legitimate printer driver from vendors like Canon, HP, or Lexmark that contains known vulnerabilities. Jake walks through analyzing vendor driver packages [32:07], demonstrating how flawed driver installer routines, arbitrary directory writes in ProgramData/AppData, and unquoted registry keys allow an unprivileged attacker to trigger DLL hijacking inside the Print Spooler service, executing arbitrary code with full SYSTEM privileges. He concludes with detection metrics and mitigation strategies for enterprise administrators.
